title: Direct integration of stretchable modules for implantable bioelectronics
authors: Yesol Kim; Hoechang Chung; Chanhui Park; Seonghyeon Nam; Sung-Hyuk Sunwoo; Dae-Hyeong Kim
matched_keywords: bioelectronics; bioelectronic; stretchable bioelectronics; implantable bioelectronics
abstract: Abstract Stretchable implantable bioelectronics enable mechanically compliant operation on deforming tissues, yet system-level integration remains challenging. Integrating electrode, interconnect, and circuit modules often requires additional adhesive or conductive bonding layers at their junctions, complicating fabrication and potentially compromising mechanical robustness. Here, we introduce an interlayer-free integration strategy that combines self-healing polymer substrates with liquid metal conductors. Healing-mediated interfacial reconstruction of the polymer substrates forms mechanically cohesive junctions within minutes of contact, while fluidic reconnection of the liquid metal establishes electrical continuity between modules. These junctions exhibit an interfacial toughness of 600 N m − 1 and maintain electrical continuity at tensile strains of approximately 1,000%. Electrode impedance and charge storage capacity show limited changes after repeated stretching. Self-healing between overlapping regions of the polymer substrate further secures electrodes wrapped around the heart and sciatic nerve. The assembled wireless systems deliver cardiac and sciatic nerve stimulation in rat models, demonstrating their stable operation in vivo. Together, these results extend self-healing beyond damage repair to system assembly and tissue fixation, enabling stretchable bioelectronics to function on dynamically moving organs.

title: Benchmarking Wearable Bioelectronics: A Multimodal Evaluation Framework Integrating Parametric Regression, Machine Learning, and Fuzzy Logic Across Domain Applications
abstract: This paper examines how a range of factors, including hardware architecture, sensor accuracy, battery lifetime, and user satisfaction, influence the performance and applicability of wearable technology. Through a study of 29 hardware and more than 2,300 hardware-enabled outcomes, we present a comprehensive analytical model, which includes ordinary least squares regression, nonlinear Random Forest feature extraction, and Takagi–Sugeno fuzzy logic inference. The models indicate that the four main performance indicators are heart rate accuracy, sleep tracking accuracy, battery life, and consumer satisfaction. Sensitivity analysis reveals that the hardware form factor is a unique technological architecture that no other hardware form factor can substitute for. title: LiSIUM – a light sheet bioimaging hub in South America
authors: Anibal A. Vargas; Luz M. Fuentealba; Alenka Lovy; Felipe A. Court; Leonardo E. Valdivia
abstract: ABSTRACT Light sheet microscopy has revolutionized biological imaging, yet prohibitive procurement costs and technical demands have restricted its availability in South America, creating a persistent technological gap for regional biomedical research. The Light Sheet Imaging at Universidad Mayor initiative (LiSIUM) has established a framework for regional access, capitalizing on a fully operational, state-of-the-art light sheet platform. In this Essay, we describe the implementation of LiSIUM and its core framework for expanding advanced imaging access across South America. This initiative has built a regional community for knowledge transfer through allocated funding, travel grants, and a structured program of international workshops, specialized courses and technical specialist support. LiSIUM provides a vital platform for high-resolution four-dimensional imaging, particularly for developmental biology, enabling investigators to address fundamental embryological questions ranging from cell fate determination to complex tissue morphogenesis. Ultimately, LiSIUM serves as a scalable model for mitigating technological disparities and empowering the next generation of researchers in resource-constrained scientific communities.

title: All 3D-Printed Conducting Polymer Hydrogel-Based Soft Surface Electromyography Electrode Array for Noninvasive Fatigue Assessment
authors: Rongtai Wan; Jie Cao; Gen Li; Yi He; Bo Zhang; Tao Lin; Baoyang Lu
abstract: Abstract High-density surface electromyography (sEMG) electrode arrays allow the recording of rich myoelectric signals and provide a useful approach for monitoring exercise-induced muscle fatigue. However, existing sEMG electrode arrays often suffer from mechanical mismatches between conventional rigid electrodes and soft tissues, as well as complex fabrication processes and limited programmability, which severely constrain the rational design and practical application of sEMG electrode arrays. Herein, we successfully fabricate an eight-channel PEDOT:PSS-PVA hydrogel-based soft sEMG electrode array via a multi-material 3D printing. Through systematic rheological characterization of the composite inks and rational design of a printable three-layer electrode architecture, we achieve seamless interfacial integration and integrated sequential fabrication. The as-prepared sEMG electrode array exhibits exceptional softness comparable to that of human soft tissues (Young’s modulus ∼ 10 kPa), low electrochemical impedance (∼22 Ω), and good electrochemical stability. Leveraging these advantageous properties, our sEMG electrode array enables noninvasive sEMG signal recording and monitoring of fatigue-associated sEMG changes with a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR > 20 dB) under various grip forces before and after exercise, and captures sEMG changes associated with fatigue progression during repetitive movements. These results validate the capability of our electrode array for high-quality sEMG monitoring of fatigue-associated electrophysiological features and open up promising avenues for future applications such as scientific athletic training.
